fdroid:com.clipvault.app.summary: ClipBoard Manager with history, selection and management. Needs LSPosed / Root
fdroid:com.clipvault.app.description:
ClipVault is a deliberately small clipboard manager: one screen with a search
bar and your copied entries, and one settings screen. Nothing else.
Tap any past entry to put it back on the clipboard - it's marked as the
active entry, and selecting it never creates a duplicate or reorders your
history.
Capture works without any of the usual clipboard-reading permissions, using
one of two builds (chosen when the app is compiled, not a switch inside it):
* LSPosed build (default) - a module hook installed into system_server reads
 clipboard writes system-wide, before Android's background-read
 restrictions even apply.
* Root/priv-app build - installed via a Magisk/KernelSU module straight into
 /system/priv-app, so a background service can read clipboard changes the
 way Android's own privileged clipboard tools do. Flash the module, reboot
 once, done.
Settings are limited to what a clipboard history actually needs:
* Private mode, to pause saving entirely
* A configurable history limit (or no limit)
* Clear history
ClipVault makes no network requests, contains no analytics or ads, and
stores everything locally on the device.
Requires either an active LSPosed module or root access to capture
anything - see the project README for setup instructions.
This app is fully AI generated. It's great though 🤷♂️
There should be two versions up on F-Droid,
the lower one using Xposed 93 and the higher one libxposed 102.
If one doesn't work maybe the other does!
It works for me on my Android 15, it should work from A13 upwards,
but users have reported it not working on A16.

fdroid:com.nitulshah.nudge.name: Nudge
fdroid:com.nitulshah.nudge.summary: Stop doomscrolling: live scroll counter, wellness score and gentle nudges
fdroid:com.nitulshah.nudge.description:
Nudge is a free, open-source Android app to help you stop doomscrolling and build healthier phone habits. It gives you a live scroll counter, a daily wellness score for your phone use, and gentle nudges when you scroll fast. It is a self-awareness tool, not a medical treatment.
WHAT NUDGE DOES
A draggable bubble floats over every app and counts your scrolls live, so you can see the number climb in real time, no matter which app you're in.
Each day gets a single Wellness Score from 0 to 100, built from your scroll volume, session length, how often you unlock your phone, your bedtime habits, and the apps you use, so a heavy day tells you why, not just that it was heavy.
Scroll fast while doomscrolling and the bubble glows amber. Keep going and you get a notification, then a full-screen prompt to take a short break. Ignoring it is always an option.
A history dashboard shows your score, scrolls, unlocks and screen time over the last 7, 30 and 90 days, along with your peak activity hour and a per-app breakdown of where your scrolling actually goes.
Pause tracking or reset your data any time, for the days you don't want Nudge watching.
PRIVACY
No account is needed, there are no ads, and there are no trackers. Nudge uses no Google SDKs and no proprietary analytics SDKs of any kind. All counting happens on your phone, and your scroll, score and history data is stored in a local database on the device.
This F-Droid build has analytics removed entirely: the opt-in analytics toggle that exists in other builds of Nudge is not present here, so there is nothing to opt into, and this build never sends anything.
PERMISSIONS
Nudge asks for the Accessibility permission because that's the only way Android lets an app notice scrolling in other apps. Nudge only listens for the signal that a scroll happened and which app it was in. It never reads screen content: no text, messages, images or passwords, and it never taps or types for you.
Nudge also asks for "Display over other apps", which is what lets the live bubble float on top of whatever app you're using. You can revoke either permission at any time in Android's settings.
OPTIONAL LAPTOP SYNC
If you want your desktop scrolling counted too, Nudge can sync with a companion Chrome extension on your laptop. This is off by default: it only runs after you explicitly pair the extension with a sync code shown in Settings. If you never turn it on, no network request is ever made.
OPEN SOURCE
Nudge is open source under the Apache License 2.0. Source code, issues and releases: https://github.com/nituls265/Nudge

RWR watches through the front camera for people looking at your screen from behind (shoulder surfers). When it sees one, it:
 pops up a card over whatever app you are using with a snapshot of the onlooker (boxed in red, with "laser eyes" showing where they look),
 posts a notification,
 saves a photo or a short video clip (for example 10 s before to 10 s after) to your gallery, and optionally to your own Immich server.
 It runs in the background and can be switched on and off from the Quick Settings panel.
 Detection 
 Head tracking : a face turned toward the screen counts as looking. Lightest on battery.
 Eye tracking : follows the irises and combines them with head pose, so it alerts only when the eyes point at the screen.
 Your own face is recognised and ignored, and faces too far away to read the screen don't count.
 A debug view shows live what the detector sees and why each face counts or not.
 Private by design 
 Detection runs on the phone , offline, with bundled open-source models (YuNet and MediaPipe Face Landmarker). No analytics, no ads, no accounts.
 Nothing leaves the phone unless you pair it with your own RWR server (Docker, open source, in the same repository). Then frames go only to your server, over TLS: detection runs there at full frame rate without draining your battery, and snapshots can be uploaded to Immich.
 The camera is always off while the screen is off. Android shows its camera indicator while RWR is watching.
 Requires Android 10 or newer and a front camera. The pop-up needs the "Display over other apps" permission.

* Optional faint chart background (24h or 7d window).
* Tap to refresh.
* Light/dark theme aware.
* If the network call fails, the widget shows "!" and posts a notification with the actual error reason (HTTP status, JSON shape, etc.) so you know what's wrong.
What this app is NOT
* No tracking. No ads. No analytics.
* No accounts, no signups, no Google services.
* Only one network host is contacted: price.cheeserobot.org. No third-party servers.
* No background services — only Android's normal widget update mechanism.
Source code

Via game options, you may alter the game to solve other digits, smaller or greater grids, hiding the operators.

- operations (add, subtract, multiply, divide)
- digits (1 to n, prime numbers, Fibonacci sequence etc.)
- difficulty (covering a increasing number of game variants)
- usage of single cells
- show or hide operators
 Things still to be done 
- not all grid variants get calculated in a reasonable time
- on-boarding is missing a tutorial
- not all game variants have been supplied with difficulty ratings yet
- calculation of next grid is not bullet proof in some rare circumstances

firefox-addons:2710717.name: Progressive Web Apps for Firefox
firefox-addons:2710717.summary: A tool to install, manage and use Progressive Web Apps (PWAs) in Mozilla Firefox
firefox-addons:2710717.description:
Progressive Web Apps (PWAs) are web apps that use web APIs and features along with progressive enhancement strategy to bring a native app-like user experience to cross-platform web applications. Although Firefox supports many of Progressive Web App APIs, it does not support functionality to install them as a standalone system app with an app-like experience. This functionality is often also known as a Site Specific Browser (SSB).
 Important: If you are having problems after updating to Firefox 158, please update the native program to v2.20.1 .
This project creates a custom modified Firefox runtime to allow websites to be installed as standalone apps and provides a console tool and browser extension to install, manage and use them.
You can check out the installation and usage instructions on our documentation website . You can also check out the project's source code and more information on the GitHub repository .
 Note: When updating to 2.17.2, you may see a popup from Firefox that the extension may now collect or transmit the browsing activity. This is because according to the Firefox Add-ons Policies, communication with the native messaging host is considered data collection and transmission. No changes regarding the actual transmission have been made. No personal data leave the computer or are sent to third parties. Browsing data (the current website and manifest URLs) is only sent to the native program when installing a web app and stored locally.
 Note: I will appreciate it if you read and participate in a GitHub discussion to suggest how to make this project more user-friendly and which features would you like the most. You can also read and participate in a GitHub discussion about the documentation website.

firefox-addons:859374.name: Tab Workspaces
firefox-addons:859374.summary: Organize your tabs into workspaces. Switch between workspaces to change which tabs are displayed at the moment.
firefox-addons:859374.description:
Organize your tabs into workspaces. Switch between workspaces to change which tabs are displayed at the moment.
This extension aims to be an alternative to Tab Groups , which is no longer supported as of Firefox 57.
 Features 
 Each tab belongs to a workspace. New tabs are automatically added to the current workspace.
 Switch between workspaces from the toolbar icon to keep your tabs organized.
 Tabs in other workspaces are safely hidden away.
 Pinned tabs are visible from all workspaces.
 If you have multiple windows open, each one has its own set of workspaces.
 Send a specific tab to another workspace from the right-click menu.
 Press Ctrl+E to open the list of workspaces, then press 1-9 to switch between using keyboard shortcuts.
 Search through your tabs in the address bar. Type "ws [text]" to begin searching. Choose a result to switch to that tab.
 Notice 
There is no way to "hide" a tab with the WebExtensions API, so when switching between workspaces the tabs are actually closed and reopened.
This has the side effect of not maintaining the tabs' history, as well as stopping whatever process is going on when the tab is closed.
If you know any better way to hide the tabs, please let me know.
 Acknowledgements 
This extension was inspired by Multi-Account Containers , which also served as a reference for some of the functionality.
Special thanks to @NicolasJEngler for designing a beautiful UI for this extension!

firefox-addons:2866321.name: Lemon New Tab
firefox-addons:2866321.summary: Lemon New Tab brings fast search, grouped quick links, bookmarks, wallpapers, themes, and sync to a local-first new tab.
firefox-addons:2866321.description:
Make every new tab feel fast, effortless, and enjoyable.
Lemon New Tab is a local-first, open-source browser extension with no additional account required. Your core settings and personalized content stay in your browser, giving you fast loading, a clean interface, and no distracting news feed or ads.
 🔍 Flexible Search 
Use Bing, Google, Baidu, DuckDuckGo, Yandex, and other search engines. Search suggestions, search history, and custom search engines help you quickly find what you need using a familiar workflow.
 🧭 Quick Links 
Automatically display your most-visited sites, or add, pin, and rearrange your own links. Organize them into groups, browse with pages or scrolling, and switch to Dock or Launchpad layouts to keep favorite sites within easy reach.
 🔖 Browser Bookmarks 
Search, open, edit, delete, and rearrange your browser bookmarks without leaving the new tab page.
 🖼 Rich Wallpaper Options 
Use Bing's daily image, an online image API, or local images and videos as your wallpaper. Extensive customization options help bring your background to life.
 🎨 Highly Customizable 
A wide range of options lets you customize the layout, theme colors, and the position and appearance of individual components. Dynamic theme colors can even be extracted from your wallpaper to create a naturally coordinated page.
 🕒 Useful Without Distractions 
Display the time, date, seconds, and lunar calendar. Enjoy a daily poem, motivational quote, or your own custom text, with one-click copying whenever you want to save it.
 ⚡ Fast and Easy to Use 
Continuously optimized for faster loading and lower resource usage, with responsive layouts and independent controls for performance and visual effects.
 🔄 Easy Backup and Sync 
Import or export your settings, or use experimental cloud sync through your browser account. There is no separate account system, making setup and everyday use more convenient.
 ⚛ Built for Trust 
Lemon New Tab is open-sourced under the AGPL-3.0 license and does not actively collect or send private data.
GitHub: https://github.com/Redlnn/lemon-new-tab-page

apple-macos:6739982067.description:
GeoCeptor has two location modes: Safari spoofing works directly in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac without cables or the Companion, while System GPS uses the free GeoCeptor Companion on a Mac or Windows PC to simulate your iPhone's location across apps. Use System GPS for privacy, browsing, and development, control GPX routes, and follow live spoofing status from your iPhone. GeoCeptor's Safari layer changes location and browser privacy signals on websites.
Key Features:
- System GPS: Simulate your iPhone's location across location-aware apps using GeoCeptor Companion on a Mac or Windows PC.
- Companion Setup: A step-by-step guide helps you pair your iPhone with your computer once over USB; then control system-wide location spoofing from GeoCeptor.
- GPX Route Playback: Import GPX routes, choose a playback speed, and pause or resume simulated journeys.
- Route Builder: Create routes in-app and play them in Safari or on your device.
- Live Route Status: Monitor system spoofing and GPX playback with Live Activities and Dynamic Island controls.
- Shortcuts & Siri: Control Safari spoofing with Shortcuts and Siri.
- Custom Location Selection: Choose any location from a global map.
- Safari Location Spoofing: Make websites see your chosen location instead of your real one.
- Timezone Spoofing: Choose any timezone to use in Safari.
- User-Agent Spoofing: Change your user agent directly in Safari.
- Locale Spoofing: Change your browser language and region settings.
- WebRTC Leak Protection & Canvas Fingerprinting Defense.
- Hardware Cloak: Prevent websites from learning your device model and hardware details.
- Spoof and Override Filters: Use allowlists or denylists, set different locations for specific websites, and choose whether sites see your exact location or a nearby point.
- Developer Ready: Test apps, websites, and location-aware experiences from different places around the world.
Note: System GPS requires the free GeoCeptor Companion on a Mac or Windows PC (the Windows version is in beta) and a one-time USB pairing; on iOS/iPadOS 16 or later, Developer Mode is required. System GPS affects location-aware apps on your iPhone, while Safari spoofing affects websites only. GeoCeptor is not a VPN and does not change your IP address. Changing the reported location does not bypass server-side checks such as IP address, payment methods, or account history. Use location simulation only where permitted by applicable terms and laws; some websites and apps may prohibit it, especially streaming, financial, and e-commerce services. You are responsible for your use.
